 By Kristian Winfield | kwinfield@nydailynews.com | New York Daily News PUBLISHED: November 11, 2026 at 7:10 AM EST | UPDATED: November 11, 2026 at 10:49 AM EST Knicks head coach Mike Brown said Jose Alvarado’s disappearing minutes aren’t a knock on the veteran point guard. It just so happens that Tyler Kolek has been seizing the opportunity stemming from Alvarado’s early-season injury.
 “We’ll go with who we go with until we feel that it’s time to go to the next guy,” Brown said after playing Alvarado just the final six minutes of New York’s 32-point rout of the Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday. “So again, it’s not anything negative right now on Jose or even Tyler when he’s out. They just got to be ready to play when their number’s called, and both of them are trying to do that.”
 Brown said both point guards have to get the Knicks into their offense, run the team, defend and do the little things that win games. For now, he said, the edge belongs to Kolek.
 “Right now, Tyler’s played pretty good basketball,” Brown said. “You know, we’ve strung some games, and, you know, again, those guys are close.”
 Kolek made the call easy Tuesday. He scored 12 points on 5-of-6 shooting with four assists and one turnover in 15 minutes and scored seven points during the second-quarter blitz that put the game away. Kolek has 40 assists to just five turnovers on the season, marking the NBA’s highest assist-to-turnover ratio through the first leg of the season.
 Alvarado, on the other hand, hasn’t scored since Oct. 23 and checked into Tuesday’s game with 6:28 left in the fourth quarter and the Knicks up on the Bucks by 28 points.
 Four months after the Knicks re-signed the Brooklyn native to a three-year deal worth about $14.4 million, Alvarado has fallen out of Brown’s rotation. He has played 15 minutes, 36 seconds over the Knicks’ last three games, all of it in the fourth quarter of blowouts, and sat the entire Nov. 7 win at Cleveland as a coach’s decision and got mop-up minutes against Milwaukee.
 Brown admitted the role reversal began with Alvarado’s injury: He sprained his left ankle and missed four straight games after the loss to Boston in the second game of the season. The backup point guard minutes have been Kolek’s ever since.
 Brown sat both down before Alvarado returned against Brooklyn on Nov. 2 and told them the order hadn’t changed, but that it could.
 “The reality is Jose got hurt. Tyler gave us some good minutes, but at the end of the day, I sat them both down and I told them: ‘Jose, you’re our backup because you ended the season as the backup, but both you guys helped us win last year. Jose in the Finals. Tyler in the Cup Finals,” Brown recalled. “So I feel like both you guys can play and contribute at a high level. So both you guys got to be ready because a change can happen at any time.’”
 The change came that night. Alvarado played 8:43 in the first half against the Nets and went scoreless. Kolek got the fourth-quarter minutes. After the next game, against Chicago, Brown made it official.
 “And so I’m gonna go with Tyler,” he said, “and if I think I need to make a change because Tyler’s not getting it done in my eyes, then I’ll go back to Jose.”
 Alvarado’s case for the job is built on June. In Game 4 of the NBA Finals against San Antonio, he scored all eight of his points in the fourth quarter on 3-of-3 shooting as the Knicks erased a 29-point deficit and won 107-106. That’s the stretch Brown keeps bringing up.
 “And both those guys, I’ve said this before, both those guys helped us win at a high level,” Brown said Nov. 4. “Tyler helped us win the NBA Cup against San Antonio in Vegas. And Jose helped us win the finals.”
 The numbers this season haven’t helped Alvarado. He has 10 points on 4-of-15 shooting, eight assists and seven turnovers in five games.
 Alvarado is making $4,439,656 this season and is under contract through 2028-29. As an offseason re-signing, he can’t be traded until Dec. 15.
 “Both he and Jose contributed last year at a pretty high level and they’ll continue to contribute going forward for us,” Brown said.
 Until then, Brown said Nov. 4, the job for the guy on the bench is the same.
 “So they just have to both stay ready and make sure that they continue to do what they’re doing,” he said. “They both, when they’re not playing, they both have done a heck of a job cheering for their teammates and trying to uplift everybody.”
 The Knicks host Cleveland in the second leg of a back-to-back at 7 p.m. Wednesday.
